OSRA is for parents and legal guardians who supervise their own children's phones. A parent creates the account in the OSRA app and pairs the child's phone with the OSRA child app. The child app is visible on the child's phone and shows that it is active. OSRA must not be used to monitor another adult or anyone you are not responsible for.
Accounts are for adults (18 or over). Children do not create accounts; a child's data belongs to the family account the parent created.
2. What the OSRA child app collects
The child app sends the following to the family's account, so the parent can see it in the OSRA app:

, including in the background: the phone's position, its accuracy and the time. It is used to show where the child is, to answer the parent's "locate now" request, and for alerts when the child arrives at or leaves a place the parent has set.
: how many minutes each app was used, total screen time, how many times the phone was unlocked, and which app is open while the screen is on. It is used for screen-time limits, schedules and reports.
: the list of apps on the phone, so the parent can set rules per app and be told when a new app is installed.
Messages in chat apps the parent chooses

: the text shown on screen in those apps, together with the chat partner's displayed name or number. Email addresses, phone numbers and other long numbers in the text are masked on the phone before anything is sent. Our server checks the text against safety rules (for example for bullying or self-harm). Text that raises no concern is discarded straight away and not stored. When text does raise a concern, a short excerpt (at most 240 characters) is stored encrypted so the parent can see why the alert was raised. The parent chooses which apps are checked during setup, and can switch each one off at any time.
: if the parent has set a list of allowed contacts, a number that is not on the list raises an alert that includes that number.
: when the child asks for more time or access to a blocked app, or presses SOS, the request or alert is sent to the parent.

: the phone's model and Android version, battery level, which OSRA permissions and protections are switched on, how many other user profiles the phone has (counts only), the version of the OSRA child app, a push-notification token, and alerts when a protection is switched off. It is used to keep the protection working, to tell the parent when something needs fixing, and to detect tampering.

read SMS or MMS messages, call logs, email, contacts, photos, videos, files or the calendar. It does not record audio. The camera is used only to scan the pairing QR code, and no image is stored or sent.

2. What OSRA is, and what it is not

OSRA is a tool that helps a parent. It does not replace a parent's own care and supervision. We do not promise that OSRA will detect every risk, block every app or website, show a location that is exact or current, deliver every alert, or work without interruption. It depends on the phone, its settings and battery, the network, and on Apple's and Google's systems, and a child may switch off or get around parts of it.
OSRA is not an emergency service. The SOS button alerts the parent; it does not call the police, an ambulance or anyone else. In an emergency, call your local emergency number.
Keep your password and your sign-in codes to yourself. You are responsible for what is done through your account, and for the parents and guardians you invite to your family.
